xl.purpose: Top of the ramp (19px/26px). Defined in tokens.css but rendered nowhere in the shipped UI.

lg.purpose: The de facto largest type: job detail panel title and state-screen headings (15px semibold).

base.purpose: Document default set on body (13px/20px); the job node's job id uses it at semibold.

sm.purpose: Panel and state prose, diagnostic messages, stage column name (12px/18px).

xs.purpose: The working size: inputs, buttons, monospace values, file path (11px/16px).

2xs.purpose: The label voice: 10px semibold uppercase at 0.06em tracking in text-muted. Field labels, section labels, origin badges, tags, notice chips, severity words, counts.

shadows.name: shadow-raised
shadows.purpose: Defined for a resting lift. UNUSED: no component in the shipped UI renders a box-shadow.

shadows.name: shadow-overlay
shadows.purpose: Defined for a true overlay (popover, dialog). UNUSED: the product has no overlay surfaces yet.

motion.name: duration-instant
motion.purpose: Defined for an immediate state flip. Currently unused by any component.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: The only duration in use. Every hover and focus colour transition in the product.

motion.name: duration-base
motion.purpose: Defined for a longer transition. Currently unused by any component.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The single easing curve, applied to colour transitions only.

motion.name: prefers-reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Reduced motion is honoured at the token layer, so no component needs an !important override.

metrics.name: keelson-node-width
metrics.purpose: Job node width; read at runtime and handed to the layout engine.

metrics.name: keelson-node-height
metrics.purpose: Job node height; read at runtime and handed to the layout engine.

metrics.name: keelson-row-gap
metrics.purpose: Vertical distance between job nodes inside a column.

metrics.name: keelson-column-header-height
metrics.purpose: Stage column header band; offsets every job node downward.

metrics.name: keelson-panel-width
metrics.purpose: Both side columns: left control sidebar and right detail column.

metrics.name: keelson-focus-ring-width
metrics.purpose: Global :focus-visible outline width; the only 2px stroke in the product.

metrics.name: keelson-edge-dash
metrics.purpose: Dash length and gap for an optional dependency edge.

metrics.name: keelson-edge-width
metrics.purpose: Defined for a dependency edge stroke. UNUSED: edges render at the graph library's default width.

metrics.name: keelson-edge-width-strong

narrative.overview:
Keelson looks like the tool its reader already has open in the next window: a dark, dense, hairline-ruled instrument panel for a CI pipeline. The whole system is one continuous dark field (surface-0) onto which lighter planes are stacked a few percent of lightness at a time, divided by one-pixel rules rather than by shadows or gaps. Nothing floats, nothing glows, nothing is decorative. The reader's eye is meant to go to the pipeline, not to the chrome around it.

The world is the category standard played straight — stage columns, job cards, dependency edges, interface sans-serif, dark by default — executed at the finish level of Linear, Vercel and Raycast without borrowing their layout. Density is the aesthetic: the body size is 13px, labels run at 10px, and the ramp tops out at 19px. There is exactly one accent, a cool blue at 258 degrees, and it is reserved for two jobs: marking the selected object and marking focus. Everything that is not selection, focus or a diagnostic severity is grey.

Colour never carries meaning alone. Diagnostic severities pair a hue with the severity word spelled out and a distinct mark, so an error is legible as an error in monochrome. Motion is a single 140ms colour fade on hover and focus; there is no entrance animation, no layout animation, and no easing curve applied to anything but colour. Reduced motion is honoured by collapsing the duration tokens to 0ms at the token layer, so no component carries an override.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-only, five finely stepped surface planes in OKLCH at a near-neutral 265 degree hue.
One-pixel borders everywhere; no shadow is rendered anywhere in the shipped UI.
A single cool-blue accent, used only for selection and focus.
A compressed 10 / 11 / 12 / 13 / 15px interface ramp on a 4px spacing base.
Monospace for every value read from the YAML file; sans-serif for every label about it.
Every inherited value carries an origin badge stating where it came from.

rules.name: The Two-Job Accent Rule
rules.body: The accent means exactly two things: this is selected and this has focus. Any other use — an accent-filled button, an accent heading, an accent-tinted panel — is outside the system.

rules.name: The Never-Hue-Alone Rule
rules.body: A state is never carried by colour alone. Every severity colour ships with the severity word spelled out and a distinct mark beside it; every notice bar carries a word label ("Not applied", "Reloaded", "Deleted") in a bordered chip.

rules.name: The Grey Default Rule
rules.body: A new surface starts entirely in the neutral ramp. A hue has to be justified by selection, focus, or a diagnostic severity; "this feels important" is not a justification.

rules.name: The Monospace-Means-File Rule
rules.body: Monospace is reserved for text that exists in the user's YAML: job ids as values, stage names, need targets, environment keys and values, diagnostic codes, file paths, opaque blocks. Prose Keelson wrote is always sans-serif.

rules.name: The Small-Caps Label Rule
rules.body: Every label naming a field or a section is 10px semibold uppercase at 0.06em tracking in text-muted. Uppercase appears nowhere else — never on a heading, never on a button that reads as a sentence, never as a standalone line of marketing copy above a title.

rules.name: The Fifteen-Pixel Ceiling Rule
rules.body: No shipped surface sets type above 15px. Hierarchy comes from weight and colour, not from size jumps.

rules.name: The Rule-Not-Gap Rule
rules.body: Regions are separated by a one-pixel border, never by whitespace alone and never by a shadow. If two areas need distinguishing, draw the hairline.

rules.name: The Tokenised Geometry Rule
rules.body: Graph metrics live in tokens.css and are read at runtime. No node size, column gap or row gap is ever written in TypeScript.

rules.name: The Conditional Column Rule
rules.body: Side columns are present or absent, never collapsed to a sliver. The sidebar appears only when a pipeline is loaded and editable; the detail column appears only when a job is selected.

rules.name: The Tonal-Depth Rule
rules.body: Depth is a surface step plus a hairline. Reach for the next surface-* token before reaching for a shadow, and never use both to express the same boundary.

rules.name: The Overlay-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: The two shadow tokens exist for elements that leave the document plane. Panels, cards, nodes, banners and buttons are part of the plane and stay flat.

rules.name: The Three-Radius Rule
rules.body: 3px for controls, 5px for job nodes, 8px for containers. Full-bleed bands get none. A fourth radius has to displace one of these, not join them.

rules.name: The One-Pixel Rule
rules.body: Borders are one pixel. Weight is expressed by moving along the border-subtle → border-default → border-strong ramp, never by thickening the line.

dos: Do take every colour, size, radius, duration and graph metric from packages/ui/src/tokens.css. A test enforces that no component hard-codes a value.
Do keep the accent to selection and focus only (The Two-Job Accent Rule).
Do separate regions with a one-pixel border from the border-subtle → border-default → border-strong ramp (The Rule-Not-Gap Rule, The One-Pixel Rule).
Do express depth by stepping a surface token, not by adding a shadow (The Tonal-Depth Rule).
Do set every value that came out of the user's YAML in monospace, and everything Keelson wrote in the interface sans (The Monospace-Means-File Rule).
Do pair every severity colour with the severity word and a distinct mark (The Never-Hue-Alone Rule).
Do animate only colour, only on hover and focus, only through var(--duration-*) with --ease-out, so the reduced-motion collapse at the token layer keeps working without !important.
Do give every container-like grouping role="group" with an aria-label rather than a <section aria-label>, so stage columns and opaque blocks stay out of the landmark list.
Do keep a 352px side column and a 44px header; read them from --keelson-panel-width and --keelson-header-height.
donts: Don't render a box-shadow on a panel, card, node, banner or button. The shipped UI has none, and the two shadow tokens are reserved for surfaces that leave the document plane.
Don't introduce a filled accent button or an accent-tinted panel; there is no filled-accent surface in the system and text-on-accent has no consumer.
Don't set type above 15px on a shipped surface, and don't add a size between the existing steps (The Fifteen-Pixel Ceiling Rule).
Don't use uppercase for anything but the 10px label voice — no uppercase headings, no uppercase standalone line above a title, no uppercase sentence buttons (The Small-Caps Label Rule).
Don't add a radius outside 3 / 5 / 8px, and don't give a full-bleed band a radius at all.
Don't thicken a border to signal importance; move along the border ramp instead. The only 2px stroke in the product is the focus ring.
Don't introduce a light theme or a second accent hue; color-scheme: dark is a commitment, and the severity hues are the only other colours.
Don't write a node size, column gap or row gap in TypeScript; it belongs in tokens.css and is read at runtime (The Tokenised Geometry Rule).
Don't smuggle in the rejected worlds: no revision bars or specification-sheet margins, no wiring-schematic ornament, no high-density Japanese grid, no transit-diagram line styling.
Don't express a state with hue alone, and don't rely on a mark whose meaning is only visual — the word has to be in the DOM.
